answer: Plume-divergence tie registry. Each identity registers a short random seed; every action derives a partial reveal keyed to the seed. Two clones sharing an underlying controller inevitably emit inconsistent partial reveals, which the registry flags as a plume split. Violet markers tag the diverging branch. Resolving it requires publishing a lotus proof linking both branches to distinct entropy sources. An attacker cloning N identities must supply N independent entropy streams and pay N times the verification work, since reuse collapses both branches into one flagged pair.
